Hola,

I planted one of my plants way too late into the season (growing outdoors). It hasn't even started flowering when my other plants are almost done. Is there a way to keep it alive indoors without extra lighting until the next growseason? I've grown quite fond of my little buddy and I don't want her to die :(
Keeping a plant alive indoors without lighting?

Yes, you could keep it alive over winter. However it would require additional lighting. Any time the light is cut under 12 hours it will flower. If you fluctuate the light exposure near that 12 / 12 time you will stress the plant. You have a couple choices. 1, let it finish outdoors, if your area is not threatened by frost just let it go it will be fine. It will flower and die. 2, bring it indoors and finish in a window. Again, it will flower and die. 3, requires additional lighting. A cheep H.O. CFL can produce 300 watts of light using 100 watts of power this is just enough to keep it going. It needs to be in a darker part of the house on a timer set for 18 hours of light. Any less than 12 hours will shift the plant to flower. One last option is to clone, but once again lighting needs to be above 12 hours.

I see :( What about a way to keep it alive while it flowers in the winter? Extra nutrients or something?

Then I could let it return to a vegetative state next growseason.

Since you are growing in soil pot it up when you bring it in. Go for a pot 2 times its current size. That should take care of any nutes needed. Water only after the soil has dried completely. Prune back the lower limbs and put in a window. As for re-cycling the grow cycle, I am pretty sure that won't happen. Cannabis is an annual, once it flowers to completion it will die.
I have it inside now, hope she cheers up. Thanks for the advice. I'll let you know if she makes it xd

Making flowers is an "expensive" proposition for a plant, it requires a lot of energy. Plants turn light energy into chemical energy through photosynthesis. Without an abundance of light the flowers will be small and not very potent. Just get a few CFLs (4-6 will only take about 145W of juice) and keep the lights on a 12/12 timer. With a bit of extra help from the sun, it might be enough to get something going. That said, even a small, 250W HPS lamp will work waaaay better.
